narrative: Material PL3__M82622E9 exhibits erratic demand with a strong bimodal distribution: active production days consume ~28,000-31,000 units while idle/weekend days record near-zero demand, yielding a high CV of 0.529. Lead times are moderately stable at a mean of 5.15 working days with moderate variability (CV=0.287), dominated by transport uncertainty. The recommended (r,Q) policy uses a safety stock of 82,090 units — sized by the Normal lead-time demand approximation at the 95% service level — and an order quantity of 363,574 units capped by the 445,664-unit storage constraint, replacing the over-provisioned SAP safety stock and the MOQ-limited order size to deliver a 75% annual cost reduction.
warnings: Order quantity capped by storage constraint: unconstrained EOQ (~1,677,433) exceeds remaining storage capacity; order quantity reduced to 363,574 units.
Lead-time observations include near-zero values (0.04-0.13 days) which may represent same-day receipts or data artefacts; these pull the mean down and inflate CV.
SAP safety stock (105,459) exceeds optimized recommendation (82,090) by 23,369 units — excess inventory tying up working capital.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The (r,Q) model is appropriate for this material because demand, while erratic, is nearly continuous (94.9% non-zero days) and the unit cost is very low, making a fixed-order-quantity approach efficient. The EOQ formula minimizes the trade-off between ordering and holding costs, and the reorder point with Normal safety stock provides the required 95% service level protection against lead-time demand uncertainty.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds hard: the unconstrained EOQ of ~1.68M units is nearly 4x the available storage. The capped order quantity of 363,574 units still achieves a good balance but means more frequent orders than the true economic optimum. If storage capacity is relaxed, substantial further cost savings are achievable.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (67,494) + safety_stock (82,090) = 149,584 which is well within max_storage_units (445,664). No infeasibility conflict.
